_about: Domain presets for palette.py: what users of a category rely on (keep), what the category does from habit (question), and a twist. Graded: the research says colour that fits the product is preferred; the logo counts say most of a category already uses the same hue. The conventions are practice unless an entry says otherwise. Checked 27 November 2026.

domains.name: Developer tools
domains.convention: Dark mode as a first-class mode, often the default; high contrast for code; one signal hue for actions and the current item; status colours that mean pass, fail, running.
domains.habit: Near-black with one neon or an electric violet; or white with Tailwind blue. Both are the category's defaults.
domains.twist: Borrow the colours of the work itself: phosphor, a diff's green and red, warning amber, a terminal theme the audience already knows, the hardware's own paint.
evidence: practice: developer tools lean dark and high-contrast with one signal hue (third-party descriptions of Linear, Vercel, Supabase)
vendor: midnight blue leads finance, healthcare and energy logos; black leads technology (Bynder, 15,388 logos)

domains.name: AI products
domains.convention: A calm reading surface for long generated text; one clear action colour; visible states for thinking, streaming and done.
domains.habit: Violet-to-blue gradients, glow and glass on near-black. Users now read them as 'another AI wrapper'.
domains.twist: Take colour from the domain the AI serves (law, medicine, code, cooking), not from 'AI'; warm paper and ink read as considered.
evidence: practice: the purple gradient is a catalogued generated look (slop.md)
research: colour judged appropriate to the product type is preferred (Bottomley and Doyle 2006, Marketing Theory 6(1))

domains.name: B2B SaaS and productivity
domains.convention: Neutral, readable surfaces for all-day use; a primary that marks actions; dense tables that need status colours and chart series.
domains.habit: Corporate blue on white grey, the colour of every other tab the user has open.
domains.twist: Pick a primary from the customer's work (a warehouse orange, a ledger green) and give a second colour a real job, such as the current filter or a highlight.
evidence: vendor: midnight blue leads finance, healthcare and energy logos; black leads technology (Bynder, 15,388 logos)
research: colours map to brand personality, blue to competence, red to excitement (Labrecque and Milne 2012, JAMS 40)

domains.name: Fintech and banking
domains.convention: Trust and exactness: steady grounds, tabular figures, unmistakable gains and losses, nothing that looks like a game.
domains.habit: Navy and royal blue, or a challenger's purple; one is the old banks, the other every neobank since 2015.
domains.twist: Deep green, brass, oxblood or teal give trust without the house blue; money's own materials (notes, ledgers, brass) are a source.
evidence: vendor: midnight blue leads finance, healthcare and energy logos; black leads technology (Bynder, 15,388 logos)
research: colours map to brand personality, blue to competence, red to excitement (Labrecque and Milne 2012, JAMS 40)
vendor: blue in over 75% of credit card logos (logo surveys)

domains.name: Crypto and web3
domains.convention: Dark trading screens, live numbers, strong up and down colours.
domains.habit: Black with neon green or purple and glow: the default the whole category shares.
domains.twist: Keep the dark ground but drop the neon: soft mint, coral or a jewel tone reads as a product, not a casino.
evidence: practice: dark with a neon accent is a catalogued generated look (fingerprint.py)

domains.name: Insurance
domains.convention: Reassurance and plain language; forms that must feel safe; clear progress through claims.
domains.habit: Blue and white with stock-photo families.
domains.twist: Warmth (marigold, apricot, warm white) with a steady deep teal reads as 'we will help', which is what a claim needs.
evidence: vendor: midnight blue leads finance, healthcare and energy logos; black leads technology (Bynder, 15,388 logos)
research: colours map to brand personality, blue to competence, red to excitement (Labrecque and Milne 2012, JAMS 40)

domains.name: Healthcare
domains.convention: Clinical clarity, calm, very high legibility; red reserved for real danger; colour never the only signal.
domains.habit: Hospital blue and white everywhere.
domains.twist: Teal, sea green or a warm ground with one human warm colour (coral, apricot) keeps calm without the institutional blue.
evidence: vendor: blue in about 85% of popular healthcare logos (99designs, reported by The Drum, 2018)
vendor: midnight blue leads finance, healthcare and energy logos; black leads technology (Bynder, 15,388 logos)
vendor: green tested well in health and wellness A/B tests (Neil Patel, 6,306 tests)

domains.name: Mental health and wellness
domains.convention: Low arousal: soft grounds, low chroma, slow motion; dark modes for night use.
domains.habit: Lavender and sage pastels with a serif, the current wellness template.
domains.twist: Colour from a real place or practice (clay, dusk, eucalyptus, a temple's ochre) and a confident deep tone, not only pastel.
evidence: practice: soft low-chroma palettes for calming products
inference

domains.name: Fitness and sport
domains.convention: Energy and progress: strong primaries, high contrast, often dark for outdoor and night use.
domains.habit: Black with neon lime or orange, every tracker's look.
domains.twist: Take the sport's own kit and ground (clay court, track red, pool blue, chalk) and keep the energy with chroma, not glow.
evidence: research: colours map to brand personality, blue to competence, red to excitement (Labrecque and Milne 2012, JAMS 40)
practice

domains.name: Education and language learning
domains.convention: Encouraging and clear; progress and streaks; correct and incorrect must read instantly; long sessions need a calm ground.
domains.habit: One cartoon green, or a primary-colour rainbow on white.
domains.twist: Colour from the subject being learnt (a country's tiles and stamps for a language, chalk and graph paper for maths) and warm, confident primaries.
evidence: research: colour judged appropriate to the product type is preferred (Bottomley and Doyle 2006, Marketing Theory 6(1))
practice

domains.name: Kids and family
domains.convention: Bright, friendly, big targets; parents also need a calmer layer for settings and payment.
domains.habit: Saturated rainbow on white with every colour at equal weight.
domains.twist: A few strong colours with a lead, and the parents' layer in a quieter ground from the same palette.
evidence: practice

domains.name: Food and restaurants
domains.convention: Appetite: warm reds, oranges, browns and creams; photographs of the food carry the page.
domains.habit: Red and yellow fast-food signalling, or cream, serif and terracotta for anything artisan.
domains.twist: Colour from this kitchen: its tiles, its signature dish, its awning, its packaging; let the food photographs set the accent.
evidence: research: colour judged appropriate to the product type is preferred (Bottomley and Doyle 2006, Marketing Theory 6(1))
practice: cream with a serif and terracotta is a catalogued generated look

domains.name: Grocery and delivery
domains.convention: Freshness, speed and scannable product grids; green and produce colours; strong add-to-cart.
domains.habit: Supermarket green and white.
domains.twist: Use the produce itself: beetroot, citrus, leaf; a second colour for offers that is not alarm red.
evidence: research: colour judged appropriate to the product type is preferred (Bottomley and Doyle 2006, Marketing Theory 6(1))
practice

domains.name: Fashion
domains.convention: The garments and photographs carry colour; the interface stays neutral and steps back.
domains.habit: Black, white and one beige, the luxury-template look.
domains.twist: A neutral that belongs to the label (a tissue paper, a shop interior) and one colour from the current collection, changed per season.
evidence: practice

domains.name: Beauty and personal care
domains.convention: Skin-adjacent warm neutrals and soft colour; product photography leads.
domains.habit: Millennial pink and gold.
domains.twist: The product's own colours (a serum's amber, a lipstick range) and a deeper tone for type and action.
evidence: practice

domains.name: Luxury and premium goods
domains.convention: Restraint, depth and a few rich colours; a lot of space; nothing that looks discounted.
domains.habit: Black and gold, or black, white and a serif.
domains.twist: Jewel tones, oxblood, deep green or the house's own material (leather, lacquer, stone) at full depth.
evidence: practice

domains.name: Home and interiors
domains.convention: Materials: wood, stone, linen, plaster; warm neutrals; rooms in photographs set the mood.
domains.habit: Beige, sage and terracotta, the interiors-blog palette.
domains.twist: Sample this brand's materials and rooms; one confident colour from a product (a lacquered chair, a tile glaze).
evidence: practice

domains.name: Travel and hospitality
domains.convention: Destination photography leads; light warm grounds; clear booking actions.
domains.habit: Sky blue and sunset orange on everything.
domains.twist: Colour from the places sold (a coast's tiles, a city's transport livery), changed by destination, with one constant action colour.
evidence: practice

domains.name: Real estate and property
domains.convention: Photographs and maps lead; trust; prices and figures readable at a glance.
domains.habit: Navy and gold, or teal and grey.
domains.twist: The city's own materials (brick, concrete, sandstone) as neutrals and one accent from its signage or transport.
evidence: practice

domains.name: Legal and government
domains.convention: Plainness, accessibility at AAA where possible, obvious focus states, no decoration; trust through clarity.
domains.habit: Institutional navy and a crest.
domains.twist: Plain grounds with one strong action colour and a signal-yellow focus (a public-service convention); for advisory firms, oxblood and ivory.
evidence: research: colours map to brand personality, blue to competence, red to excitement (Labrecque and Milne 2012, JAMS 40)
practice: public-service design systems use a yellow focus ring (for example GOV.UK)

domains.name: Climate, energy and sustainability
domains.convention: Nature and optimism without cliché; data and charts carry the argument.
domains.habit: Leaf green on white with a globe.
domains.twist: Energy's own colours (solar orange, copper, grid yellow) beside a deep green, or the landscape of one place.
evidence: vendor: midnight blue leads finance, healthcare and energy logos; black leads technology (Bynder, 15,388 logos)
practice

domains.name: Media, news and publishing
domains.convention: Text first: high contrast for long reading, one strong colour for the masthead, sections or breaking news.
domains.habit: Cream, a serif and a red; the editorial template.
domains.twist: A section or masthead colour from the publication's own history or city; colour coding by section with a lead hue.
evidence: practice: cream, serif and red is a catalogued generated look

domains.name: Music, gaming and entertainment
domains.convention: Dark, immersive grounds; artwork and media lead; colour can be loud.
domains.habit: Neon on black with glitch effects.
domains.twist: The artwork's own palette per release or game; a house colour that is not neon green or violet.
evidence: practice

domains.name: Creative tools and design
domains.convention: A neutral canvas so the user's work is the colour; the chrome steps back; one tool colour for selection.
domains.habit: Grey chrome and a blue selection.
domains.twist: A playful palette in the marketing and the empty states, and a quiet one in the canvas; a selection colour that is the brand.
evidence: practice
